3045: The final panel discussion of the day on ‘Financial Services’, moderated by Prof. R Srinivasan, Chairperson, CDPG, IIMB, with Abhisar Sharma, NeSL Asset Data Limited; BG Mahesh, Sahamati; and Ramakrishna NK, Rang De, brought the focus to how account aggregation, combined with non-financial data such as gig-platform transaction records, could widen credit access for MSMEs and first-time borrowers with no formal credit history. Panellists, however, cautioned that these iterative public solutions must be matched by fair pricing and consumer awareness to avoid predatory lending. “For me, in five years, in any form of financial services, irrespective of the licence, it should happen only through AA by design, not through mandate," said BG Mahesh. Summing up the discussion, Prof. R Srinivasan noted: “We've been so focused on responsible lending that we have not focused on responsible borrowing”.

3051: The first panel discussion as part of the ‘Commerce’ track was moderated by Bachi Allamsetty from Networks for Humanity, with Karthikeyan Arumugam, DIGIIT Business Services; Ravi Haldipur, eSamudaay; and Rishi Agrawal, TeamLease RegTech. The panel coalesced around the view that open digital networks and shared infrastructure are lowering barriers to entry for smaller enterprises, while leaving product innovation and pricing to market forces. Discussions centred on the emerging concept of “Enterprise DPI”, arguing that India's enterprises, unlike its citizens, still lack a single reusable digital identity, forcing them to navigate a maze of disconnected registrations and compliances.
